title: Severe respiratory fatigue and tachypnoea in acute hypercapnia
summary: A 65-year-old man with acute severe COPD exacerbation is working intensely with rapid shallow breathing.
rationale: High resistive load and impending muscle fatigue (fatigue 0.35, spontRate 30, expResistance 18). Tests prompt initiation and adequate titration of the IPAP-EPAP gradient (pressure support) to offload respiratory pump failure and prevent invasive intubation.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: Adequate pressure support titration (IPAP-EPAP delta) to alleviate respiratory muscle fatigue

source: Davidson AC, et al. BTS/ICS guideline for ventilatory management of acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Thorax 2016;71 Suppl 2:ii1-35; teaching-convention

changes.vignette: Male 65, severe resistive work of breathing, tachypnoeic at 30/min, diaphoresis.

spontRateBpm.reason: Compensatory respiratory rate driven by acid load

pmusAmplitudeCmH2O.reason: High neuromuscular effort near exhaustion threshold

patient.presentingStory: Admitted 6 hours ago with an acute exacerbation of COPD. The ward nurse requests an urgent review: he is sweating, breathless at rest, and unable to finish a sentence. Current oxygen: 2 L/min via nasal cannula.
patient.history: Severe COPD (FEV1 35% predicted), heavy smoking history (45 pack-years), previous ICU admission for NIV 2 years ago. Full escalation agreed.

findings.examine: Diaphoretic, anxious, seated upright grasping the bed rails. RR 30, marked sternocleidomastoid activation and intercostal indrawing. Loud expiratory polyphonic wheezes bilaterally with prolonged expiratory phase. Trachea midline.
findings.cxr: Bilateral hyperinflated lung fields with tubular heart contour. No pneumothorax or consolidation.
